rationale: A tov-opener comparative ("Better is a dry morsel with quietness", web:Prov.17.1) sets a plain meal eaten in quiet against a house full of sacrificial feasting eaten amid strife, closed by its own comparative clause with nothing carried into 17:2. The root of חֲ֭רֵבָה is pointed here as "dry (morsel)" (פַּ֣ת חֲ֭רֵבָה, "a dry piece of bread"), not the sword sense the same root carries elsewhere in the book — a live homograph split (5 verses book-wide, mixed senses); the pointed vowels, not the bare consonants, decide the sense at this verse. (oshb:Prov.17.1)
rejected_alternative: Clustering with 17:2 is rejected: the two verses share no repeated token or construction — 17:1 closes its own comparison and 17:2 opens an unrelated social-inversion scenario.
observed_substrate_signals: homograph pointed as "dry", not the sword sense
device_notes: Better-than couplet; construct-noun pileup ("house full of sacrifices of strife") supplies the negative half of the comparison.

rationale: A one unified clause states a social reversal — a servant who deals wisely will rule over a shame-causing son and share in the inheritance among the brothers — with no antithetic vav dividing it and nothing continuing into 17:3.
rejected_alternative: No shared token or construction connects this verse to 17:1 or 17:3; the three maxims remain independent.
device_notes: Merit-over-birth-order maxim; one unified claim, not two contrasted cola.

rationale: Two parallel similes — a crucible for silver, a furnace for gold — supply the vehicle for a tenor withheld until the closing colon: Yahweh tests hearts. The metaphor is completed within the verse itself.
rejected_alternative: No catchword ties this verse to 17:2 or 17:4; the metalworking simile and the divine-name clause belong to this verse alone.
observed_substrate_signals: exact token (one of two ch.17 occurrences)

rationale: Synonymous parallelism restates one act twice: "an evildoer heeds wicked lips" becomes "a liar gives ear to a mischievous tongue", the same attentive listening named with different subject-nouns and different speech-nouns, closed within the verse.
rejected_alternative: No catchword bridges this verse to 17:3 or 17:5.

rationale: Two independent maxims share one verse, bound only by a shared theme of scorn rather than a repeated word: mocking the poor reproaches the Maker, and gladness at another's calamity will not go unpunished.
rejected_alternative: Cluster with 17.4 or 17.6 is rejected — no token repeats across either seam.
device_notes: Juxtaposition rather than vav-adversative contrast.

rationale: A chiastic pair of construct phrases — "crown of old men", "glory of children" — trades its generational nouns (grandchildren, then parents) across the line, closing the reciprocity thought within the verse.
rejected_alternative: No shared token links this verse to 17:5 or 17:7.
device_notes: Synthetic; no vav-conjunction pivot.

rationale: An a-fortiori clause ("much less") moves from a minor case — excellent speech ill-fitting a fool — to a major one — lying lips still less fitting a prince — within one argument.
rejected_alternative: No catchword links this verse to 17:6 or 17:8.
device_notes: One escalating argument, not two independent claims.

rationale: One sustained metaphor — a bribe as a precious stone in its giver's eyes — carries the whole verse to its gnomic result clause, "wherever he turns, he prospers"; nothing hands off to a neighboring verse.

rationale: Concealment is set against repetition in an antithetic pair: covering an offense promotes love, but repeating a matter separates close friends, closed on its own vav-adversative.
device_notes: One of the chapter's antithetic-texture verses (+ adversative clause, 3 of 28 verses this chapter).

rationale: A comparative frames rebuke against beating: a rebuke sinks deeper into a man of understanding than a hundred lashes into a fool, closing on the numeral with no further clause.
rejected_alternative: No catchword ties this verse to 17:9 or 17:11.
device_notes: Comparative maxim complete in one clause.

rationale: The verse states cause and consequence within itself — an evil man seeks only rebellion, so a cruel messenger is sent against him — the causal link internal, not carried into 17:12.
device_notes: WEB's own “only” (web:Prov.17.11) renders the adverb; a self-contained gnomic claim.

rationale: A rather-than comparison prefers meeting a bear robbed of her cubs to meeting a fool in his folly; the comparison closes on its own two nouns and does not continue into 17:13.
rejected_alternative: No catchword bridges this verse to 17:11 or 17:13.

rationale: A fixed-retribution claim closes the verse — rewarding evil for good means evil will not depart from one's house — a self-contained maxim carrying a ketiv/qere pair at its verb.
device_notes: Retribution maxim; K/Q resolved at the same verb that carries the verse's whole claim.

rationale: An extended metaphor — releasing water opens strife — resolves into its own admonition, "stop contention before quarreling breaks out", the whole warning closed within the verse.
device_notes: Synthetic; imperative-style close ("leave off") belongs to this verse alone.

rationale: Two legal-reversal clauses — justifying the wicked, condemning the righteous — are fused by "both of them alike" into one abomination-verdict naming Yahweh, the fusion phrase closing the unit.
observed_substrate_signals: exact token (second of two ch.17 occurrences)

rationale: The verse is framed as a rhetorical question — why money in a fool's hand to buy wisdom, since he lacks understanding? — an interrogative form distinct from the declaratives around it, closed by its own causal clause.
rejected_alternative: No catchword bridges this verse to 17:15 or 17:17.
device_notes: Rhetorical-question maxim, self-contained.

rationale: A synonymous doublet — "a friend loves at all times" restated as "a brother is born for adversity" — completes its own claim about steadfast attachment.
rejected_alternative: Clustering with 17:18 is rejected even though both verses carry the root (17:17's "the friend" and 17:18's "his neighbor"): 17:17 praises covenant loyalty while 17:18 warns against a contractual pledge before a ‘fellow’ — the same root in two different registers, not a repeated construction.
device_notes: Synonymous doublet (friend/brother); no vav-contrast.

rationale: A specific legal folly is named — striking hands and becoming collateral before one's neighbor — and nothing continues the thought into 17:19.
rejected_alternative: Cluster with 17:17 is rejected for the register-split reason disclosed at that verse; no separate construction reaches into 17:19 either.
device_notes: Self-contained legal-folly vignette.

rationale: Two independent maxims share the verse — loving strife and building a high gate — both diagnosed as self-destructive ambition, joined without a vav-contrast; the repeated אהב verb is internal anaphora, not a cross-verse catchword. (oshb:Prov.17.19)
device_notes: Two-maxim verse on self-ruinous ambition.

rationale: A perverse heart's failure to find good is paired with a deceitful tongue's fall into trouble — two clauses on the same subject-type closed within the verse.
device_notes: Synthetic double-consequence verse.

rationale: A near-synonymous restatement — fathering a fool brings grief, and the father of a fool has no joy — names the same relationship twice with different predicates.
device_notes: Restatement, not antithesis.

rationale: An antithetic couplet — a cheerful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones — completes its own body-effect contrast.
device_notes: Healing-vs-desiccation contrast, part of the chapter's antithetic texture.

rationale: The verse names a specific corrupt transaction — a bribe taken in secret to bend the paths of justice — closed by its own infinitive purpose-clause.
device_notes: Self-contained corruption vignette.

rationale: An antithetic contrast of gaze — wisdom sits before the discerning man's face, but the fool's eyes roam to the ends of the earth — closes on the spatial image of wandering eyes.
rejected_alternative: Clustering with 17:25 is rejected: both verses carry the token "fool," but 17:24's fool is an unfocused onlooker while 17:25's is the subject of a father's grief — the shared noun names two different roles, a thematic echo rather than a repeated construction.
device_notes: Antithetic gaze-contrast (focused wisdom vs. wandering folly).

rationale: A foolish son is diagnosed as a double grief — bitterness "to his father" and to "her who bore him" — the parallel dative phrases closing the verse's own complaint.
rejected_alternative: No further cluster is adopted at this seam (see 17:24's disclosure of the shared token).

rationale: The verse states two wrongs as one class — punishing the righteous is not good, nor is flogging officials for their integrity — a doubled "not good" judgment closed by its own גם-clause. (oshb:Prov.17.26)
device_notes: Synthetic double-wrong verse.

rationale: The verse commends verbal restraint — one who spares his words has knowledge, one of even temper has understanding — closing on its coordinate noun, with a ketiv/qere pair at its second predicate.
device_notes: Restraint maxim; K/Q resolved at the predicate adjective.

rationale: The paradox that even a fool who stays silent is counted wise closes chapter 17 on its own concessive גם-clause, with no construction reaching across the chapter boundary into 18:1. (oshb:Prov.17.28)

rationale: A self-isolating man is diagnosed as pursuing appetite against all sound judgment — one complete character-portrait closed on its own verb יתגלע. (oshb:Prov.18.1)
device_notes: Self-isolation diagnosed in one unified clause.

rationale: A contrast of interest closes on its own כי אם ("but rather") clause — a fool has no delight in understanding, taking pleasure instead in revealing his own opinion. (oshb:Prov.18.2)
device_notes: Interest-contrast maxim, self-contained.

rationale: A chain of three abstract nouns — wickedness brings contempt, and with dishonor comes disgrace — closes the verse on its own escalation, the doubled גם markers doing the internal linking. (oshb:Prov.18.3)
device_notes: Three-noun chain-reaction verse.

rationale: Deep waters supply the image for a man's mouth, and a flowing brook for the fountain of wisdom — two similes on speech closed within the verse. rationale: Partiality toward the wicked's face and depriving the innocent of justice are named as one "not good" judgment, closed within the verse.
rejected_alternative: No shared token with 18:4; cluster with 18:6 is rejected — the construction that binds 18:6-18:7 is named at that row instead.
device_notes: Not-good judgment on judicial partiality.

rationale: The two verses run a matched, reversed construct chain on the exact same head noun כְ֭סִיל "fool": 18:6 opens שִׂפְתֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל "lips of a fool" and closes וּ֝פִ֗יו "and his mouth," while 18:7 opens the mirrored פִּֽי כְ֭סִיל "mouth of a fool" and closes וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו "and his lips" — an exact body-part chiasm (lips…mouth // mouth…lips) built on the repeated noun כסיל, naming one two-verse portrait of the fool's speech (strife and blows in v.6, ruin and a snare in v.7). observed_substrate_signals: exact skeleton token repeated at the same construct-chain slot
device_notes: Body-part chiasm across the seam; parallelism class synthetic (consequence intensifies from strife/blows to ruin/snare).

device_notes: Hazard disclosure: despite the verse-initial match, the tier-1 header spine names only 30:1 and 31:1 as collection headers — 18:8 is explicitly excluded from header function; parent_collection remains C2, no seam sits here.

rationale: Slackness at one's work is classed as brotherhood with a master of destruction — one equivalence-claim closed within the verse.
device_notes: Self-contained equivalence maxim.

rationale: The pair runs an the exact same construct-noun-of-strength phrase twice for opposite referents: 18:10's מִגְדַּל עֹ֭ז "tower of strength" belongs to Yahweh's name and closes וְנִשְׂגָּֽב "and is set safe," while 18:11's קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ "city of his strength" belongs to the rich man's wealth and closes נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה "exalted" — but only "in his own imagination" (בְּמַשְׂכִּיתֽוֹ). Both the strength-noun (עז/עזו) and the exalted-noun (נשגב) recur across the seam, an antithetic construction run contrasting a true refuge with an imagined one. (oshb:Prov.18.10; oshb:Prov.18.11)
rejected_alternative: Independence is rejected because the second verse's phrase is built to invert the first's claim word-for-word, not merely echo its topic; reading 18:10 alone would lose the ironic twist that ‘his own imagination’ supplies.
observed_substrate_signals: two shared roots, both recurring bare and suffixed at the same syntactic slot
device_notes: Antithetic construction run; true security (divine name) vs. false security (wealth) built on the same construct pattern.

rationale: An antithetic before-clause pair — before destruction the heart is proud, but before honor is humility — closes on its own reversal of sequence.
device_notes: Sequence-reversal maxim (pride precedes fall, humility precedes honor).

rationale: Answering before listening is named folly and shame in one self-contained judgment, with a temporal בטרם-clause closing the thought. (oshb:Prov.18.13)

rationale: A man's own spirit sustaining him in sickness is set against the unanswerable question of who can bear a crushed spirit — the verse closes on its own rhetorical מי-question. (oshb:Prov.18.14)
device_notes: Antithetic-by-outcome couplet; the second half is unanswerable rather than declarative.

rationale: Synonymous doubling: the discerning heart acquires knowledge, the wise ear seeks knowledge — the same acquisitive act named twice with different organs.
device_notes: Acquisitive doublet; internal, not cross-verse, repetition.

rationale: A gift's social effect — making room, bringing its giver before great men — is stated as one unified consequence, closed on its own verb ינחנו. (oshb:Prov.18.16)

rationale: The verse warns that the first pleader in a dispute seems right until his opponent comes and cross-examines him — a self-contained legal-process maxim with a ketiv/qere pair at its verb.
rejected_alternative: No shared token with 18:16 or 18:18; cluster with 18:18 is rejected — the pairing that binds 18:18-18:19 is named at that row instead.

rationale: The exact same plural noun מִ֭דְיָנִים "contentions/disputes" is the subject of 18:18a ("the lot settles מִ֭דְיָנִים") and reappears as the qere reading of 18:19's own K/Q pair (ketiv ומדונים, qere וּ֝מִדְיָנִ֗ים) describing disputes "like the bars of a fortress" — the exact same lexeme repeated unchanged across the seam, moving from disputes resolved by lot (v.18) to disputes that outlast reconciliation once a brother is estranged (v.19). (oshb:Prov.18.18; oshb:Prov.18.19)
rejected_alternative: Independence is rejected because the second verse's key noun is not a generic synonym but the exact same inflected form of the first verse's operative noun, an exact-repetition catchword rather than a mere thematic echo; a construction this exact outweighs the chapter's typical thematic drift.
device_notes: Catchword chain across the seam; lot-resolved disputes vs. unresolvable estrangement.

rationale: A man's stomach is filled by the fruit of his own mouth, his own lips' harvest satisfying him — a self-consuming-speech image closed within the verse.

rationale: A man's own folly subverts his way, yet his heart rages against Yahweh instead — an ironic self-contradiction closed on its own vav-clause.

rationale: An antithetic couplet — wealth adds many friends, but the poor is separated even from his friend — closes on its own comparative reversal.

device_notes: Two-verse elaboration of mercenary friendship; the weaker of this part's clusters, resting more on discourse-logic (dependency) than on an exact repeated lexeme.

rationale: Getting wisdom is named self-love, and keeping understanding is said to find good — two acquisitive clauses on the same subject closed within the verse.

rationale: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who utters lies shall perish — restating 19:5's opening colon with a harsher closing verb, closed within itself; the WLC marks a petuchah after this verse.

rationale: The exact same noun אִשָּֽׁה/אִשָּׁ֥ה "wife/woman" closes the second colon of both verses in direct antithesis: 19:13's מִדְיְנֵ֥י אִשָּֽׁה "a wife's quarrels" (a continual dripping, alongside "a foolish son" in the first colon) against 19:14's אִשָּׁ֥ה מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת "a prudent wife" (from Yahweh, alongside "house and riches" as merely human inheritance in the first colon). matching bicolon frame (inheritance colon + wife colon)
device_notes: Antithetic wife-pairing across the seam (quarrelsome vs. prudent, human inheritance vs. Yahweh's gift).

rationale: Slothfulness is said to cast a man into deep sleep, and the idle soul will hunger — two consequence-clauses on laziness closed within the verse.

rationale: Direct-address counsel — listen to counsel and receive instruction, that you may be wise in your latter end — closes on its own purpose clause.
